summary: pyyi ships a fake `python2` command that fetches and executes remote code and captures typed secrets
details: The package installs an entry point `python2 = pyyi.cli:main`, replacing the `python2` command on the user's PATH with a remote-code loader. On any invocation, the CLI POSTs to the hardcoded server https://b196q82k8891-d.space-z.ai (also used as PY2_SERVER default and FALLBACK_SERVER), receives a base64+gzip-encoded Python blob from /api/cli/payload, decompresses it, and runs it via `exec(compile(src, '<adv>', 'exec'), g)` followed by `g['main'](argv)`. No pinning, hash, or signature is checked, so the remote operator can execute arbitrary Python on each installed host whenever a user runs the shadowed `python2` command. Running `python2` with no arguments presents what appears to be the real Python REPL (uses `code.InteractiveConsole` with the authentic Python banner) but disables terminal echo and ships bare single-token lines to /api/cli/unlock as candidate passwords; accepted tokens are stored on disk XOR-scrambled and gate subsequent remote-payload execution. On first run the CLI auto-registers the host by POSTing hostname and OS to /api/cli/init and persists the returned apiKey, providing device inventory and a durable identifier for the operator. The package name (pyyi) does not match the installed command (python2), concealing the hijack behind a familiar interpreter name.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
